title: Turn soft transparency into hard edges

seo.metaTitle: Crisp Hard Edges for PNG - Free, Runs Locally
seo.metaDescription: Snap every semi-transparent pixel to fully on or fully off with one threshold, from 0 to 100 percent, while colors stay untouched. Free, no signup, no upload.
seo.longDescription: Turn soft transparency into hard edges makes transparency a decision instead of a gradient: each pixel's opacity is compared with the Alpha threshold, and everything at or above it becomes fully opaque while everything below becomes fully transparent. Semi-transparent pixels snap to one side or the other, colors are left untouched, and the picture ends up with crisp, unfiltered edges — the same look a mask-based cutout has. The whole pass runs in your browser.
facts: Runs entirely in your browser: no upload, no server, no signup.
Alpha threshold from 0 to 100 percent; a pixel exactly at it stays visible.
Colors are never touched — only the fourth channel is rewritten.
Soft shadows and anti-aliased rims collapse; feathering is the opposite operation.
Free with no daily limit, no watermark and no account, also for commercial use.
howTo: Drop the image with soft edges into the source area, or pick a file from your device.
Set Alpha threshold; 50 splits the opacity range in half.
Lower it to keep more of the soft rim, raise it to cut the rim away.
Download the result as PNG - JPG has no alpha channel to store it.

faq.q: What happens to a pixel at exactly the threshold?
faq.a: It becomes fully opaque. The rule is that a value at or above the threshold goes on and anything below it goes off, so 50 leaves every pixel with 50 percent opacity or more visible.

faq.q: Will the edges look smooth afterwards?
faq.a: No, they look hard. The soft ramp collapses into a hard rim with a visible staircase along a diagonal, and feathering is the opposite of what this tool does.
A shadow lives in the semi-transparent range, and hardening sends everything below the threshold to fully transparent. Lower the threshold to keep it, or keep the shadow by feathering instead.

faq.q: Does it change the colors of the picture?
faq.a: No. Red, green and blue are copied through untouched and only the fourth channel is rewritten. Use the show transparent areas tool first to see which pixels are about to flip.
